output.query: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease versus autoimmune encephalitis cortical ribboning

results.finding: Updated sporadic CJD criteria added MRI high signal in the caudate and putamen or in at least two cortical regions on DWI or FLAIR.
Patterns of DWI and FLAIR hyperintensity, read with ADC maps, distinguished prion disease from non-prion rapidly progressive dementia.
CSF RT-QuIC has a specificity close to 100% for sporadic CJD and was added to the diagnostic criteria; a negative result argues against CJD.
results.source: Hermann P et al. Lancet Neurol 2021;20:235-246

output.summary: Cortical DWI hyperintensity occurs in sporadic CJD and in non-prion rapidly progressive dementias, including autoimmune encephalitis; the pattern, the ADC and CSF RT-QuIC help separate them.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 negative; onconeural and other neuronal-surface antibodies negative; sodium 134 mEq/L after correction
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, metabolic panel, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, onconeural and neuronal-surface antibody panels and a cell-based serum IgG anti-GluN1 assay read with the CSF
action_criteria.rationale: At 61 the other neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies and the metabolic causes of an encephalopathy after recent hyponatraemia must be tested.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left temporo-parietal, insular and pulvinar cortical FLAIR and DWI hyperintensity without ADC reduction or enhancement
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, stroke, osmotic demyelination and structural causes before LP, and shows the cortical pattern that raises CJD.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal cell count, absent bands, HSV and SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative, RT-QuIC negative, CSF anti-GluN1 positive at 1:4
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR, RT-QuIC for prion disease and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: Serum is negative and the cell count normal, so the CSF assay carries the diagnosis; RT-QuIC addresses the CJD-like MRI.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild generalized theta slowing only; no seizures, periodic discharges or extreme delta brush
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: Drowsiness and a fluent aphasia need an EEG to exclude non-convulsive seizures and to look for periodic sharp-wave complexes of CJD.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No tumour in the chest, abdomen or pelvis
action_criteria.label: Screen for an underlying tumour with contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
action_criteria.rationale: At 61 and a former 20 pack-year smoker the tumour risk is mainly carcinoma, which CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis covers.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid hyperglycaemia on metformin and IVIG thrombotic and renal risk
action_criteria.label: Optionally check his metformin, antihypertensives and aspirin against the planned immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Useful for steroid hyperglycaemia on metformin and IVIG risks in an older diabetic man, but not a diagnostic step.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis after COVID-19 and on CJD mimics
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; it is not a clinical step and nothing in the work-up depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges). Monitor capillary glucose and adjust his diabetes treatment during the steroid pulse (HbA1c 7.4% on metformin).
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumour: at 61 and a former smoker, repeat tumour screening during follow-up if the course is refractory or the disease relapses.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide.
Neurology-led care with speech and language therapy for the aphasia.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.

accepted: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis following COVID-19 (CSF-positive, serum-negative)

differential.key_features: CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR negative; the intrathecal SARS-CoV-2 IgG reflects the recent infection, and the CSF anti-GluN1 antibody gives a specific diagnosis. Respiratory illness was mild.

differential.diagnosis: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) or VZV encephalitis
differential.key_features: Left temporal involvement raises it, but CSF HSV-1, HSV-2 and VZV PCR are negative two weeks into the illness, the cell count is normal and there is no haemorrhage or enhancement.

Cortical ribboning raises it, but the signal is unilateral without ADC reduction or caudate and putamen involvement, CSF RT-QuIC and 14-3-3 are negative, the EEG has no periodic sharp-wave complexes and onset followed an infection by days.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-A, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX or IgLON5)
differential.key_features: The serum neuronal-surface panel is negative and the CSF anti-GluN1 assay is positive.

differential.diagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke in the left MCA territory
differential.key_features: Fluent aphasia and vascular risk factors raise it, but the deficit progressed over 10 days, the signal is cortical without ADC reduction and extends to the pulvinar outside one arterial territory, and there are no motor signs.

differential.diagnosis: Osmotic demyelination syndrome or hyponatraemic encephalopathy
differential.key_features: The language and behavioural change began on day 5, before the low sodium was found on day 9, persisted after correction, and the MRI shows no pontine or extrapontine myelinolysis.

differential.diagnosis: Non-convulsive status epilepticus with peri-ictal MRI change
differential.key_features: Routine and 24-hour EEG show mild slowing only, without seizures or periodic discharges.
Apathy and low mood do not explain a fluent aphasia with alexia and agraphia, drowsiness, cortical MRI change and a positive CSF antibody.

key_clinical_evidence: Onset over 10 days, beginning about 5 days into mild COVID-19, of behavioural change with apathy, a fluent aphasia with paraphasias, alexia and agraphia, and drowsiness: 3 of the six Graus 2016 groups.

CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:4) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016). The diagnosis rests on this CSF assay: serum is negative (as in about 14%, Gresa-Arribas 2014), the cell count is normal and oligoclonal bands are absent.

MRI left temporo-parietal, insular and pulvinar cortical FLAIR and DWI hyperintensity without ADC reduction; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds, and here it excludes structural causes, stroke and osmotic demyelination.
CSF RT-QuIC and 14-3-3 negative and no periodic sharp-wave complexes: the cortical ribboning does not indicate CJD.
EEG mild generalized slowing without seizures; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis, and a near-normal EEG does not exclude it.
CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumour; earlier immunotherapy is associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses. Here CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR is negative and the intrathecal SARS-CoV-2 IgG reflects the recent infection.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild COVID-19 (fever, dry cough, positive RT-PCR) beginning about two weeks before admission.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests SARS-CoV-2 or another viral encephalitis, or COVID-19 delirium, and delays antibody testing.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Unilateral cortical signal without ADC reduction or striatal involvement, a course of days after an infection, negative RT-QuIC and 14-3-3 and no periodic sharp-wave complexes do not support CJD; cortical signal change occurs in autoimmune encephalitis.
red_herrings.data_point: Cortical ribboning with DWI hyperintensity in the left temporo-parietal cortex and insula.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Serum is negative in about 14% of patients; the CSF assay is the reference test and is positive here.
red_herrings.data_point: Negative serum anti-GluN1 IgG on cell-based assay.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent to exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis and settle on a seronegative autoimmune encephalitis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatraemia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis. Here the deficits began before the low sodium was found and persisted after correction, and the MRI shows no myelinolysis.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild hyponatraemia (sodium 134 mEq/L) after correction of a low sodium at the outside hospital.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a hyponatraemic encephalopathy or osmotic demyelination.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A fluent aphasia with alexia and agraphia and drowsiness is neurological; it needs MRI, EEG and CSF before any psychiatric diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Apathy, withdrawal and low mood with incomprehensible speech in a previously independent 61-year-old.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on depression or a primary psychiatric disorder.

sequence_constraints.reason: Imaging before LP in a patient with seizures or altered consciousness; CT head is an acceptable alternative, so the constraint is soft.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure 16 cmH2O. WBC 3 cells/uL (100% lymphocytes); RBC 0/uL. Protein 66 mg/dL (mildly elevated). Glucose 101 mg/dL (ratio 0.60, serum 168 mg/dL). Gram stain: no organisms; culture: no growth. HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV and SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative. SARS-CoV-2 IgG index 3.2 (reference <1.0) and spike protein antibodies positive. Oligoclonal bands absent; IgG index 0.58. IgG anti-GluN1 (NMDA receptor) antibodies positive, titre 1:4, on cell-based assay. RT-QuIC and 14-3-3 protein negative. Cytology: no malignant cells.

contraindications: Class warning: haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists are associated with severe neuroleptic intolerance (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis) in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
interactions: Metformin + methylprednisolone: steroid-induced hyperglycaemia; monitor capillary glucose and adjust diabetes treatment.
Metformin + IV iodinated contrast: no change needed at a creatinine of 1.1 mg/dL; withhold for 48 hours only if eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or acute kidney injury develops.
IVIG (maltose-containing preparations) can falsely raise glucose readings on glucose dehydrogenase (GDH-PQQ) meters.
Amlodipine and tamsulosin: additive hypotension with sedatives; no interaction with the proposed immunotherapy.
Aspirin: no interaction with methylprednisolone at 81 mg beyond additive gastrointestinal risk; consider gastric protection during the steroid pulse.
Aciclovir: no interaction with his medicines; maintain hydration (crystal nephropathy).
Levetiracetam or lacosamide + current medicines: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction.
warnings: Sulfonamide allergy (rash): no sulfonamide in the proposed immunotherapy or antivirals.
Rituximab: screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before the first dose.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumour removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

No central pontine or extrapontine myelinolysis
No periventricular white matter lesions suggestive of demyelinating disease
Paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear

metadata.condition_name: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis following COVID-19 (CSF-positive, serum-negative)
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: cortical ribboning on MRI mimics CJD, temporal involvement raises HSV encephalitis, a recently corrected low sodium suggests osmotic demyelination, the recent COVID-19 and intrathecal SARS-CoV-2 antibodies suggest a viral or post-viral encephalopathy, and the serum anti-GluN1 assay, cell count, oligoclonal bands and EEG are normal or near normal: only the CSF anti-GluN1 assay gives the diagnosis. The age (61-year-old man) adds further complexity.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions, 5 red herrings, subtype=RP; requires the CSF antibody with a negative serum result, RT-QuIC for the CJD-like MRI, EEG, labs and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; viral, prion, vascular and metabolic mimics compete with the diagnosis.
metadata.revision_reason: Independent Reviewer 2 anti-NMDAR audit: tumour screening tailored by age/sex and moved out of lab payloads; paired serum/CSF anti-GluN1 reachable; routine EEG baseline with selected continuous escalation; blanket CAP CT, FDG-PET and blood cultures removed

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive behavioral changes, incomprehensible speech, and drowsiness over the past 10 days

family_history: Father: ischemic stroke at age 72, deceased
Mother: type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism
Brother: coronary artery disease, stent placement at age 58
No family history of autoimmune disease or psychiatric illness
past_medical_history: Hypertension, diagnosed 8 years ago, well controlled on amlodipine
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed 5 years ago, managed with metformin
Benign prostatic hyperplasia, managed with tamsulosin
COVID-19 infection confirmed by RT-PCR approximately 2 weeks prior to presentation

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in a single-story home; independent in all ADLs prior to this illness
social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (20 pack-year history)

patient.history_present_illness: A 61-year-old unvaccinated man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with progressive behavioral abnormalities and language dysfunction over the past 10 days. The illness began approximately two weeks ago with mild fever, dry cough, and general malaise. A SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test on the second day of illness was positive, and the patient was advised to quarantine at home with supportive care. His respiratory symptoms were mild and did not require supplemental oxygen. However, on approximately the fifth day of illness, his wife noted that he began making unusual comments, speaking in an irrelevant and sometimes incomprehensible manner, and appearing increasingly withdrawn and apathetic. Over the ensuing days, his language deterioration worsened progressively. He began producing jargon-like speech with frequent word substitutions and appeared unable to understand simple questions or follow basic instructions. His wife reports that he stopped reading the newspaper and could no longer write notes, activities he previously performed daily. He also became increasingly drowsy, spending most of the day sleeping, and showing little interest in his surroundings. There were no witnessed seizures, no limb weakness, no abnormal limb movements, no gait difficulty, and no bladder or bowel incontinence. There were no headache, neck stiffness, or photophobia reported. The patient was initially evaluated at an outside hospital on day 9 of illness, where he was found to have low serum sodium and was started on correction per institutional protocol. Despite normalization of his sodium levels over several days, his behavioral and language abnormalities persisted without improvement, prompting referral to the current institution on day 15. His wife specifically denies any recent changes in medications, no new substance exposures, and no prior history of psychiatric illness. She notes he was in his usual state of health and cognitively intact prior to the onset of respiratory symptoms.

neurological_exam.additional: No signs of meningismus. No orofacial dyskinesias or autonomic instability noted at presentation. Low mood and apathy prominent. No asterixis.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing intact bilaterally. No dysmetria or intention tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive 3mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Face symmetric. Hearing grossly intact to finger rub bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline. No dysarthria appreciated despite language disturbance.
neurological_exam.gait: Steady, narrow-based gait. Tandem walking intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but apathetic with flat affect. Oriented to person only; disoriented to place, time, and situation. Speech is fluent with preserved grammar and repetition but shows prominent paraphasias (semantic and phonemic), circumlocutions, jargon, and perseveration. Comprehension of simple commands is severely impaired; cannot follow two-step commands. Unable to read or write (alexia and agraphia). Pattern consistent with transcortical sensory aphasia. Attention and concentration difficult to assess due to language barrier. MMSE not obtainable due to comprehension deficits.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone in all extremities. Strength 5/5 throughout upper and lower extremities bilaterally. No drift on pronator testing. No fasciculations or involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric throughout. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities. No extinction to double simultaneous stimulation.
